The 16-segment fingerprint contains the rectangular drive enclosure and internal sine-wave glyph while excluding feeder, breaker, conductor, pump, and schedule geometry. The second drive reproduces it exactly at score 1.000.

The two modules sit only 344 pixels apart among nearly parallel electrical branches. Their exact VFD-P-12 and VFD-P-13 text boxes prove one-to-one local tag ownership; the P-12/P-13 load labels and neighboring AHU disconnect branch cannot steal either placement.

The page also contains a large electrical equipment schedule and a repeated symbol legend. Neither is traversed by table logic, and neither manufactures placements: this remains a production symbol-sweep and tag-assignment test with no file, page, or coordinate special case.

review.method: Full-page H-601 control-diagram review plus engine-resolution audit of all seven unique rooftop-unit digital-input callouts, their duplicate equipment-side references, and sibling I/O types.

The generic OI-AI-1 legend example, controller rectangles, equipment raster, switches, wiring, notes, and symbol-table graphics are excluded. The behavior is driven by exact local tag ownership, not a filename, page, coordinate, or project rule.

review.method: Full-page E-603 ladder-diagram review plus engine-resolution audit of every W pilot-light glyph across all three independent HVAC controller circuits.
notes: This extended-campaign case uses the pilot-light convention rather than the document's baseline relay coils. The chlorine-dioxide low-speed RUN LOW lamp is the seed; RUN HI and the running lamps in the two other controller circuits are the three non-seed repeats.

Each 36-segment symbol combines the circular lamp, internal W glyph, and four short light rays. All four physical instances reproduce exactly across separate ladder positions and different surrounding contacts, wires, and annotations.

The internal W identifies the graphical convention, not an installed asset ID, and the adjacent RUN LOW, RUN HI, and RUNNING phrases are operating-state prose. Null label fields therefore preserve honest symbol counts without inventing equipment tags.

Relay/contactor coils, F fan coils, selector contacts, thermostats, timer switches, remote controller contacts, terminals, and wiring junctions remain excluded by the complete lamp geometry. No source-specific exception participates.

review.method: Full-page M-201 controls review plus engine-resolution audit of the constant-volume and dedicated-outdoor-air inline supply-fan bodies and the richer VAV fan assembly.

The schematic names the AHU systems in their captions rather than attaching a literal equipment tag to either tight fan body, so null labels are intentional. No nearby CV, DPS, TS, HS, AI, AO, DI, or DO tag may rename a fan.

review.method: Full-page M6.01 system-architecture review plus engine-resolution audit of the complete 27-module VLC-853-E controller bank across three BACnet trunk rows.
notes: This extended-campaign case uses compact BAS application-controller modules rather than the document's baseline roof-plan condensing-unit fan assemblies. The F-B1 module is the seed and all 26 non-seed VLC-853-E modules are frozen individually.

The six-segment fingerprint captures the controller enclosure and clipped lower corner while excluding the BACnet trunk, drop lines, equipment addresses, terminal marks, title graphics, and larger control-panel details.

Every enclosure contains both a host-equipment identity such as F-B2, RTU-B4, or OAU-B1 and the repeated controller model VLC-853-E. The latter is the correct swept-device family: choosing a host tag would incorrectly split identical controller hardware by the equipment it serves.

The bank exercises 27 one-to-one text claims, three independent trunk rows, one geometry variant at score 0.762, repeated model labels, and unique address lines. Exact VLC-853-E text boxes are frozen so one token cannot satisfy multiple controller placements.

review.method: Full-page M4.1 chilled-water controls review plus engine-resolution audit of the three installed temperature-transmitter assemblies and the surrounding relay, pump, and BAS point symbols.
notes: This extended-campaign case uses temperature-transmitter assemblies rather than the document's baseline bypass control valves. The chilled-water tank transmitter is the seed; the chiller entering- and leaving-water transmitters are the two non-seed repeats.

A circle-only seed produced two exact but semantically wrong CR/CSR control-relay bubbles. The reviewed 34-segment fingerprint includes the TT body and its connected thermowell/stem, eliminating those generic-circle false positives by geometry rather than by a document exception.

The two chiller transmitters are quarter-turned contextual variants at score 0.946 with substantial adjacent piping linework. Their exact local TT text boxes corroborate both physical placements despite the richer connections.

DI/DO/AI point callouts, motor circles, CR/CSR relays, current sensors, VFDs, pumps, flow switch, equipment tags, sequences, and title graphics remain excluded. The sheet-level scope preserves the set-wide rule that reference control diagrams are not installed-plan counts.

review.method: Full-page M-801 airflow-diagram review plus engine-resolution audit of all 12 same-convention supply, return, and exhaust fan bodies across ACU-A-1 through ACU-A-6.

The tight 79-segment fingerprint captures the fan scroll, inlet hub, and discharge transition. All 12 placements score 1.000 despite mirrored return/exhaust orientation, different connected coils and dampers, and varying surrounding duct geometry.

Quarter-turned FA, HCA, CC, and H equipment tags are printed inside upstream inline component rectangles. Text-height scaling now uses the lettering axis, and rotated equipment marks cannot chase connected duct as an annotation leader, preventing CC-A-1 and H-A-3 from renaming adjacent fans.
